Summary On November 12, Indonesia's rupiah reached a record low against the dollar, driven by expectations of interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve.
 As Asia's worst-performing currency this year, it weakened to 18,253 to the dollar, prompting intervention from Indonesia's central bank.
 The decline coincided with the resignation of the country's vice president amidst a diploma scandal, compounding challenges for a government already under pressure from economic discontent, corruption issues, and wildfire crises.

 Subscribe HONG KONG, Nov 12 — Indonesia’s rupiah hit a record low against the dollar on Thursday as traders rushed into the US unit on expectations the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates into the new year.
 Asia’s worst-performing currency this year weakened to as much as 18,253 to the greenback in afternoon trade, spurring the Indonesian central bank to intervene to provide support.
 The drop came just before the country’s vice president resigned in the midst of a scandal over his high school diploma, adding to pressure on a government facing widespread dissatisfaction over the economy, graft and wildfires. — AFP
